title: Cut the number of Git processes a task-sync command starts, so commands stay well inside their deadlines on Windows
outcome: Cut the number of Git processes a task-sync command starts, so commands stay well inside their deadlines on Windows
acceptance: The number of Git subprocesses started by each slow task-sync path (the memory sync refusal that took more than 10 s alone, the destination and Publisher::publish setups that hit their 60 s and 120 s limits) is measured on Windows, with per-call cost and total, from evidence rather than estimate

Each measured path starts a bounded number of Git processes that doesn't grow with unrelated repository or history size, and the task_sync_cli and destination suites finish on Central well inside their unchanged deadlines
No deadline is raised and no assertion is weakened; a test counts the Git processes a representative command starts and fails if the count regresses
